conclusion: Setting beta := normLower makes the rung-3 grid site inequality true by construction and the cell obligation eps' + L*h/2 <= beta still holds at all 200 cell endpoints, in ball and in chained-rect arithmetic, with no statement weakened. But docs/25 4.3's prediction that the cell condition then carries >= 10x slack is wrong: measured exactly in rationals the worst obligation clears by 1.3697x (ball) and 1.3566x (chained rect) against 1.3647x before, so the remedy moves the worst case by under 1% in either direction, and it is additionally contingent on porting scripts/60's emission to composite chains, because in the non-chain arithmetic it emits today normLower is 0.17-0.55x pred_beta and the cell condition fails at every obligation measured.
confidence: High on the two headline numbers and on the refutation. The cell obligation is read straight off the Lean lemma DH_lower_on_[hv]cell rather than modelled, and it was evaluated in exact rationals over the committed plan, so 1.3697x is not a floating-point judgement; the ball betas come from the already-committed 215-site run and the chained-rect betas were recomputed here at all 104 sites in a structurally different arithmetic, agreeing with pred_beta to under 1% at every one. Lean-side, no Lean source was changed, so the axiom audit is unchanged by construction; the cold-toolchain lake build reached 8801 of 8803 targets and lost two heavy unrelated modules (ChebyshevBounds, Pub1.CertAtoms) to out-of-memory kills while sharing the container with this hunt's sweep, so green was not observed here and is not claimed. SETTLED 2026-08-17 after close: the unfinished rebuild was run to completion on an idle 64 GB machine against the same origin/main (ba657c7) with lean/ byte-identical to it -- all 8803 targets built, exit 0, zero error lines, and CertAtoms elaborated in 27m33s against the 733s at which it was killed. The two kills were the container, not the proofs; the hunt's refusal to say green on the evidence it had was correct. Bounds the memory a clean build needs from above on one machine only; CI headroom is still unmeasured. Weaker on two points, both stated in RESULTS.md: the non-chain failure row is a 12-site thinnest-first sample rather than a census, and no generated grid site was compiled end to end (one site is roughly seven minutes of kernel time, the full certificate an 18-hour build), so what is verified is the mirror arithmetic and the obligation algebra, not a kernel-checked instance of the new beta literal.

core_candidates.what: A generation-time check that the downstream obligation a literal feeds can actually be paid, not just that the literal is true
core_candidates.why_reusable: The defect here was not a wrong number, it was a true inequality that measured nothing because its right-hand side had been drawn at the achievable bound. Any generator that emits a bound and hands it to a later lemma can hide the same way. The fix is three lines: derive the literal from the measurement, and assert the consumer's hypothesis where the literal is emitted

notes_for_operator: Case-log entry landed as Hunt #40 in hunts/README.md; #40 was free (the log ran to #37). The operator addendum names 'the Pub1 Lean files' as the work area, but rung 3 does not live in lean/ZetaLean/Pub1 -- it is DHAssembly / DHCertSupport / DHZeroCriterion / DHDemo directly under lean/ZetaLean, and the per-site files are generated by scripts/60 into an output directory that is not in the build at all. That is the template mismatch to note. No Lean source needed changing for this remedy, so lean/ is untouched. No collision with the other two live lanes: nothing under hunts/frontier_math was read or written. Lean environment had to be built from nothing in this container (no elan, no toolchain); elan install plus Mathlib cache fetch plus a full lake build took roughly a third of the run's wall clock, which is worth knowing when budgeting any Lean-touching hunt here. The container is 4 cores / 15 GB and cannot run a full lake build alongside an exact-rational sweep: ZetaLean.ChebyshevBounds and ZetaLean.Pub1.CertAtoms were both OOM-killed (exit 137) under contention and both cleared the same point when rerun idle. Worth scheduling Lean builds and heavy Python sweeps serially here.
